testCases.name: test_case_0
testCases.input: Design an AI architecture assistant that generates an initial architecture, asks a human architect for approval, incorporates human feedback when revisions are requested, and produces a final blueprint only after approval.
testCases.actualOutput:
# Archon Finalizer – AI Architecture Assistant Blueprint --- ## 1. System Overview The **AI Architecture Assistant** is an agentic, human‑in‑the‑loop (HITL) platform that: 1. **Generates** an initial software architecture from user‑provided goals and requirements. 2. **Presents** the draft to a human architect through an interactive UI. 3. **Collects** explicit approval or structured feedback. 4. **Iteratively refines** the architecture until the human architect grants approval. 5. **Produces** a formal, immutable blueprint (LaTeX) that is delivered to the user only after approval. All interactions are fully traceable, and the system can support an arbitrary number of revision cycles while guaranteeing that no final blueprint is emitted without human consent. --- ## 2. Requirements Summary | Category | Requirement | |----------|-------------| | **Functional** | • Generate an initial architecture from goals/requirements.
• Present the draft to a human architect for review.
• Allow the human to **Approve** or **Request Revisions**.
• Incorporate human feedback to iteratively refine the draft.
• Emit a formal final blueprint **only after explicit approval**. | | **Non‑functional** | • **Traceability** – maintain a complete revision & feedback history.
• **Accuracy** – output must be technically coherent and follow standard architectural patterns.
• **Usability** – seamless, intuitive interaction loop for the human architect. | | **Constraints** | • HITL is mandatory; the system cannot finalize a blueprint autonomously.
• Unlimited revision cycles must be supported. | --- ## 3. Architecture & Major Components | Component | Responsibility | Key Interactions | |-----------|----------------|------------------| | **User Interface (UI)** | React‑based front‑end for goal entry, architecture visualization (Mermaid.js), feedback submission, and final blueprint download. | ↔ UI ↔ Architecture Generation Engine, Feedback Processor, Blueprint Generator | | **Architecture Generation Engine** | Calls the selected LLM (GPT‑4o / Claude 3.5) to produce an initial or revised architecture diagram and description. | Receives goals / revision instructions → returns architecture artefacts | | **Feedback Processor** | Parses human‑written feedback (spaCy / HF Transformers) into structured, actionable instructions for the Revision Engine. | Receives raw feedback → emits structured revision payload | | **Revision Engine** | Orchestrates a new generation pass: injects revision instructions, preserves prior context, and triggers the Generation Engine. Implemented with **LangGraph** (agentic workflow). | Consumes structured instructions + prior state → calls Generation Engine | | **Blueprint Generator** | Transforms the approved architecture into a formal LaTeX document (including Mermaid diagrams rendered to SVG). | Receives approved architecture → outputs PDF/LaTeX bundle | | **State Manager** | Persists session state, revision history, and approval status. Uses **PostgreSQL** for relational data + **MongoDB** for flexible document storage. | All components read/write session & revision records | | **Event Sourcing Layer** | Guarantees immutable audit trail of every event (goal submission, generation, feedback, revision, approval). Implemented with **Apache Kafka** topics per session. | Publishes events → consumed by State Manager & optional analytics | | **Workflow Orchestrator** | Coordinates the overall HITL loop, enforces the approval gate before Blueprint Generation, and handles retries. Implemented with **Apache Airflow** (or **Prefect**). | Drives state transitions, schedules tasks, monitors timeouts | | **Security & Auth** | Centralized authentication/authorization via **Auth0** (OAuth2/OIDC). Enforces role‑based access (e.g., architect vs. viewer). | Protects all API endpoints and UI routes | | **Infrastructure** | Containerized services (Docker) deployed on **Kubernetes** for scaling, health‑checks, and rolling updates. | Provides resilience and horizontal scalability | > **Note:** The diagram below (Mermaid) visualizes the high‑level component relationships. ```mermaid graph TD UI -->|Submit goals| GenEngine GenEngine -->|Initial architecture| UI UI -->|Approve / Feedback| FeedbackProc FeedbackProc -->|Structured instructions| RevEngine RevEngine -->|Trigger| GenEngine GenEngine -->|Revised architecture| UI UI -->|Approval| BlueprintGen BlueprintGen -->|Final LaTeX| UI UI -->|All events| Kafka Kafka -->|Persist| StateMgr StateMgr -->|Read/write| Airflow Airflow -->|Orchestrates| UI Auth0 -->|Auth| UI & APIs ``` --- ## 4. Technology Stack | Layer | Recommended Technology | Alternatives (for future decisions) | |-------|------------------------|--------------------------------------| | **Front‑end UI** | React + TypeScript + Material‑UI (MUI) | Vue.js, Svelte | | **Diagram Rendering** | Mermaid.js (client‑side) | GoJS, D3.js | | **Real‑time Collaboration** | Socket.IO (WebSocket) | Liveblocks | | **LLM (Generation Engine)** | OpenAI GPT‑4o **or** Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet | Mistral Large, Llama 3.1 405B | | **Feedback NLP** | spaCy **or** Hugging Face Transformers | Rule‑based regex/keyword matching | | **Agentic Revision Engine** | LangGraph (agentic workflow) | CrewAI, Temporal.io | | **Workflow Orchestration** | Apache Airflow **or** Prefect | Temporal.io | | **Blueprint Generation** | LaTeX (PDF output) | Markdown + Pandoc, DocxTemplate | | **State Management** | PostgreSQL (relational) + MongoDB (document) | Redis (self‑hosted) | | **Event Sourcing** | Apache Kafka (topic per session) | NATS | | **Authentication / Authorization** | Auth0 (OAuth2/OIDC) | Keycloak | | **Containerization & Orchestration** | Docker + Kubernetes | Vercel, AWS Amplify | | **Observability** | Prometheus + Grafana (metrics), Loki (logs) | – | | **CI/CD** | GitHub Actions (build, test, deploy) | – | All selected technologies satisfy the functional, non‑functional, and constraint requirements while keeping the architecture coherent. --- ## 5. End‑to‑End Data Flow 1. **Goal Capture** - Architect enters goals/requirements in the UI. - UI emits a **`GoalSubmitted`** event to Kafka and stores the payload in PostgreSQL. 2. **Initial Architecture Generation** - Airflow triggers a **`GenerateArchitecture`** task. - Generation Engine calls the LLM with the goals → returns architecture description + Mermaid diagram. - Result is persisted, a **`ArchitectureGenerated`** event is published, and UI displays the draft. 3. **Human Review** - Architect clicks **Approve** or writes **Feedback** in the UI. 4. **Feedback Path (Revision Loop)** - **Feedback** → UI sends raw text to Feedback Processor. - Feedback Processor parses the text → produces structured instructions (e.g., “replace component X with Y”). - A **`FeedbackProcessed`** event is emitted. - Revision Engine receives the structured payload, merges it with prior context, and re‑invokes the Generation Engine. - New architecture is stored, a **`ArchitectureRevised`** event is emitted, and UI presents the revised draft. 5. **Approval Path** - When **Approve** is selected, UI sends an **`ApprovalReceived`** event. - Airflow validates that the session is in an *Approved* state (enforced gate). - Blueprint Generator consumes the approved architecture, renders LaTeX (including embedded SVG diagrams), and produces a PDF/LaTeX bundle. - **`BlueprintCreated`** event is emitted; UI offers a download link. 6. **Traceability** - Every event (GoalSubmitted, ArchitectureGenerated, FeedbackProcessed, ArchitectureRevised, ApprovalReceived, BlueprintCreated) is stored in Kafka and mirrored in PostgreSQL for audit queries. 7. **Error & Retry Handling** - Airflow task retries on transient failures (LLM timeouts, network errors). - Human is notified via UI toast messages; session state remains consistent. --- ## 6. Security & Compliance Considerations | Concern | Mitigation | |---------|------------| | **Authentication** | All UI and API endpoints protected by Auth0 (OAuth2/OIDC). Tokens validated on each request. | | **Authorization** | Role‑based access control (RBAC): only users with the *Architect* role can approve or submit feedback. | | **Data Confidentiality** | TLS 1.2+ for all in‑transit traffic. Sensitive session data encrypted at rest in PostgreSQL (pgcrypto) and MongoDB (field‑level encryption). | | **LLM Data Handling** | Use provider‑specific data‑privacy settings (e.g., OpenAI’s “no‑store” flag) to prevent model training on proprietary architecture data. | | **Auditability** | Immutable Kafka log + signed event metadata (HMAC) to guarantee tamper‑evidence. | | **Compliance** | Design aligns with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 principles (access control, logging, data protection). | | **Input Validation** | UI sanitizes all user‑generated content; server‑side validation prevents injection attacks. | | **Rate Limiting** | API gateway (e.g., Kong) enforces per‑user request quotas to protect LLM usage costs. | --- ## 7. Scalability & Reliability Considerations | Aspect | Strategy | |--------|----------| | **Stateless Services** | Generation Engine, Feedback Processor, Revision Engine, Blueprint Generator are containerized stateless micro‑services; can be horizontally scaled behind a load balancer. | | **Stateful Stores** | PostgreSQL and MongoDB are deployed in HA clusters (primary/replica) with automated failover. | | **Event Bus** | Kafka cluster with replication factor ≥ 3 ensures durability and high throughput for concurrent sessions. | | **Workflow Engine** | Airflow workers can be autoscaled; DAGs are lightweight, enabling many concurrent revision cycles. | | **Caching** | Frequently accessed static assets (e.g., UI bundles, diagram SVGs) served via CDN. | | **Observability** | Prometheus scrapes metrics; Grafana dashboards alert on latency spikes, task failures, or queue backlogs. | | **Graceful Degradation** | If LLM service is unavailable, UI shows a friendly “generation temporarily unavailable” message; existing sessions remain accessible. | | **Cost Control** | Token usage limits per session enforced in the Generation Engine; fallback to cheaper open‑source LLMs if budget thresholds are exceeded (future decision). | --- ## 8. Important Implementation Considerations 1. **Prompt Engineering** – Design robust system prompts for the LLM that include: - Goal context - Prior architecture snapshot (as Mermaid code) - Structured revision instructions (e.g., JSON) 2. **Feedback Parsing** – The Feedback Processor must map natural‑language comments to deterministic actions (add/remove component, change interface, modify technology stack). A fallback to human clarification may be required for ambiguous feedback. 3. **Session Identification** – Every user interaction is tied to a **Session ID** (UUID) that propagates through Kafka events, DB rows, and Airflow DAG runs. 4. **Versioning** – Store each architecture revision as a separate document with a version number; enable UI “history view” for traceability. 5. **Diagram Rendering** – Mermaid diagrams are generated server‑side (via `mermaid-cli`) to produce SVGs for inclusion in LaTeX. 6. **Approval Gate Enforcement** – The Blueprint Generator task is **conditionally triggered** only when the session state flag `approved = true`. Airflow’s `BranchPythonOperator` can enforce this. 7. **Testing Strategy** – - Unit tests for NLP parsing and LLM prompt templates. - Integration tests for the full HITL loop using a mock LLM endpoint. - End‑to‑end UI tests (Cypress) covering approval and revision cycles. 8. **Observability Hooks** – Emit custom metrics (e.g., `revision_cycle_count`, `average_generation_latency`) for capacity planning. 9. **Deployment Pipeline** – CI pipeline builds Docker images, runs security scans (Trivy), pushes to a private registry, and triggers a Helm upgrade on the Kubernetes cluster. --- ## 9. Assumptions & Open Decisions | Assumption / Open Decision | Details | |----------------------------|---------| | **LLM Provider SLA** | It is assumed that the chosen LLM (GPT‑4o / Claude 3.5) offers sufficient uptime and latency for interactive use. A fallback to an open‑source model is not yet provisioned. | | **Maximum Revision Depth** | No hard limit is defined; operationally, a configurable max‑cycle count (e.g., 20) may be added to prevent runaway loops. | | **User Roles** | Only a single “Architect” role is considered; future extensions may include reviewers, auditors, or external stakeholders. | | **Diagram Complexity** | Mermaid is assumed sufficient for the expected architectural diagrams; extremely large or custom diagram types may require a switch to GoJS/D3.js. | | **Compliance Scope** | The blueprint is treated as non‑PII; if future use cases involve regulated data, additional controls (e.g., data residency) will be required. | | **Cost Monitoring** | No explicit budgeting component is
